# Analysis

```{r}
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
library(survival)
```

```{r}
load(projr::projr_path_get("raw-data", "processed", "data_surv_tidy.rda"))
data_surv_tidy <- tibble::as_tibble(data_surv_tidy)
data_surv_tidy |>
  UtilsDataRSV::view_cols()
data_surv_tidy <- data_surv_tidy |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    regimen = factor(data_surv_tidy$regimen, levels = c("oral", "cab_la"))
  )
```

```{r}
cox_fit <- survival::coxph(
  survival::Surv(start, stop, event) ~
    regimen + age_yrs + base_egfr + risk_score + strata(site_id),
  data = data_surv_tidy
)
```

- Regimen is a time-varying covariate, so we prevent immortal time bias
- Time-varying exposure is properly accounted for, as regimen switches for the interval and the interval is given the correct length
  - We could have started all intervals at time zero (rather than modelling a two-year baseline hazard), but there isn't time here for that.
- Included seemingly-relevant baseline confounders
  - We have many visits per subject, so we do not have too many confounders per person
- We could have accounted for site by a standard confounder, but we can also allow each site to have its own baseline hazard, as we did here.
  - This would be appropriate if the shape of the baseline hazard differs between sites.
- We could have fit a parametric survival model, but that entails an additional assumption about the shape of the baseline hazard. Under time constraints, we choose the more flexible model.


```{r}
summary(cox_fit)
```

- The LA regimen is highly statistically signfiicant (p = 0.0012), and decreases hazard ratio by 77.74%, approximately (95% CI: 44.90%, 91.09%).

- It appears as thought the constant hazard ratio for age is rejected (0.0091), possibly declining over time, but the PH assumption for regimen seems fine (p = 0.2928).

```{r}
cox_zph <- cox.zph(cox_fit)
```

```{r}
var_vec <- c("regimen", "age_yrs", "base_egfr", "risk_score")
path_vec <- c()
for (x in var_vec) {
  path_p <- projr::projr_path_get("cache", paste0("p-cox-resid-", x, ".png"))
  path_vec <- c(path_vec, path_p)
  png(path_p)
  plot(cox_zph, var = x)
  dev.off()
}
```

- To check for correct functional form, I would plot the residus (`resid(cox_fit)` against the explanatory variables), and see if there's a pattern (e.g. the residuals systematically increase or decrease with the covariate), which would indicate a mis-specified functional form.
- To check for influential observations, I would look at the `dfbeta` (change in the estimated regression coefficient) for treatment against each observation, and see if any single observation has an especially large effect.
